_comment: Ordered dispatch queue for everything not yet done. `after` names dispatch slugs (from dispatch.json) or queue ids that must land first. `conflicts` names slugs whose files overlap — do not run both at once. Six concurrent agents is the ceiling: four agents plus the orchestrator hit the session limit twice on 2026-09-06, and the cap is usage, not wall-clock.

units.title: Four follow-ups the third integration round routed onward
units.note: 1. SECURITY, and the real fix for a hole caught during integration: p1-018's --everywhere grant is gated on OperationSpec::names_nothing(), reasoning that an operation naming nothing can only reach the endpoint pinned when its credential was stored. P1-002 landed the first counterexample -- cloudflare.account.read declares no resource AND no params, yet resolves its account from the project's own apex.toml (bound: GET /accounts/{id}; unbound: GET /accounts), so `*` would let an agent in a project the owner never approved read that project's account. p1-018's own test caught it and the integrator fixed it with an explicit allow-list shared by the gate and the CLI hint. That is fail-closed but the registry test will pass SILENTLY for the next such operation. The real fix is `same_everywhere` as a declared fact on OperationSpec. Consequence of the interim fix: cloudflare.account.read is per-project only. 2. SECURITY: broker.rs's run_curl invokes a bare `curl` off PATH with no -q, while setting HOME to the owner's -- so a root daemon's curl reads the owner's ~/.curlrc. api.rs already uses /usr/bin/curl -q. 3. cloudflare/api.rs should move onto broker::run_curl, but this is a FEATURE not a resolution: run_curl returns curl's exit code rather than the HTTP status the Cloudflare Reply model needs, and appends stderr onto the body, which breaks its status parse. Fix run_curl first. 4. p1-018 shipped no docs: neither `apex mcp connect` nor --everywhere appears under docs/, though the refusal message and the CLI hint point users at both.

units.title: Make an APEX machine actually verify the signature it already has
units.note: P1-047 measured this rather than suspecting it. /etc/containers/policy.json on both machines is byte-identical to the image's /usr/etc copy and holds one insecureAcceptAnything, and the booted deployment records the consequence in its own origin: container-image-reference=ostree-unverified-registry:. Every image is cosign-signed and self-verified in CI and none of that reaches a machine. The .sig tag is present for the digest both machines run and names build-image.yml@refs/heads/main; the .att tag is not, because the SBOM work has only ever been built on roadmap/v2.2. DANGEROUS TO GET WRONG: a policy that refuses the wrong thing leaves a machine unable to update, and on an atomic OS that is not a small mistake. Whoever takes this must prove the rollback path on katana BEFORE the L16 ever sees it, must keep a documented escape hatch, and must not enable enforcement in the same change that introduces the policy. cosign is not in the image; skopeo and openssl are.

units.note: Both are already implemented on task/p0-013-request-origin and land as `partial`. P0-014's remainder is a real FIDO/WebAuthn path behind --origin-policy remote. P0-015's remainder is that nothing reports lock state: APEX Shell locks with ext-session-lock and never calls SetLockedHint, so logind reports LockedHint=no on a session locked for an hour. The shell half was recovered from a WIP snapshot and pushed as fix/locked-hint at 87c84f3 (LockedHintService.qml, qmldir, Lockscreen.qml wiring) — integrate that first. units.note: 26 of section 13.2's 32 operations remain after P1-002 took seven. Two framework gaps the Cloudflare author hit and worked around locally, which P1-005 should fix generally rather than repeat: Bound carries no provider payload, so bind cannot hand what it resolved to perform — Cloudflare re-resolves and refuses on mismatch, but git does NOT, which makes git's host pin a TOCTOU rather than a guarantee; and mint cannot reach a companion service, which is why OAuth refresh could not be expressed as mint and why P1-011 will hit the same wall.

Two policy scope questions stay open on purpose -- LLMNR accepted on every interface, and mDNS accepting unicast from any source. Also open: katana's installed apex predates the firewall subcommand, and whether the page should stop offering commands that image cannot run is a judgement nobody has made. ALSO, from the P2-005 agent, measured with positive controls: a hotspot cannot work under the shipped policy, three independent ways -- forward is policy drop, the DHCP rule matches replies rather than a client's DISCOVER, and port 53 is shut. The exception mechanism itself is sound (631/445/2049 reopen immediately). And two lines in `apex devices network` state the current policy as fact and go stale the day it changes; ping task/p2-005-device-maturity when the policy moves.
